source.title: What the "Spotless" Mind Remembers: How Knowledge Entanglement Shapes What Leaks After Unlearning in LLMs
source.authors: Aakriti Shah; Yi-Fan Hu; Thai Le

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; some tables and figures are flattened in the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether rephrased prompts and changes to prompt entanglement alter recall after unlearning, using a different attack and measurement setup from the claim’s cited studies.
record.gate_note: The paper tests rhetorical prompt framing and an intervention that changes prompt wording and entanglement. It does not test fine-tuning attacks, activation ablation, quantization, or a counter-method. Figure 2’s detailed cells are not separately extracted; the paper’s reported aggregate correlation ranges are recorded. Results cited from other studies are not included.
record.test_reason: The study applies prompt-only attacks (authority framing, plus entity-specific rewrites that preserve meaning) to WHP- and GA+KL-unlearned models, and reports factual recall against the direct-query baseline (Table 3, Table 2). It also reports suppression and capability retention (Table 10). These bear on A and E with a different attack and measurement setup from the originals.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that entanglement predicts and causally shapes leakage after unlearning: the correlation weakens but survives under WHP and inverts under GA+KL. They read this as WHP suppressing output over intact pathways while GA+KL more closely resembles erasure. They also report that persuasive framing shifts recall by up to several-fold, and propose a pre-unlearning predictor (AUC up to 0.834) for leakage triage.
record.recipe_differences: The study implements WHP and GA+KL unlearning and evaluates persuasive prompts and graph-based entanglement; its central intervention is prompt rewriting, not the fine-tuning, activation-ablation, quantization, or prompt-attack recipes named in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The relationship and prompting effect differ by unlearning algorithm; WHP and GA+KL show opposite effects of raising or lowering prompt entanglement. Domain, model, and framing also vary; authority framing is not uniformly beneficial.

fits_no_version.finding: Correlation between a prompt's graph-entanglement score (M9) and factual recall is r≈+0.39 to +0.51 at base, stays positive but weaker under WHP (+0.16 to +0.33), and flips negative under GA+KL (−0.14 to −0.25) in all 8 domain×model cells. The authors read this as WHP suppressing output while GA+KL disrupts retrieval pathways.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Output-level unlearning (WHP) preserves the structure of which facts leak, while gradient-ascent unlearning inverts it; the entanglement–recall correlation diagnoses suppression versus disruption.

record.problems: No chance-level benchmark is stated. The authors test only two unlearning algorithms, two domains, and four models; scale correlations use four models per cell. Prompt variants were generated with GPT-4 and only a sample was checked; response evaluation relies on LLM judges calibrated with human labels.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted under the 60-row limit. Detailed per-cell Figure 2 correlations were not extracted because the supplied figure text is flattened; the paper’s reported aggregate correlation ranges are included.

untested.parts: Near-chance accuracy on a multiple-choice benchmark; attacks other than prompting.
All: no relearning or fine-tuning attack.
All: no activation ablation or internal representation analysis; only behavioural correlations with a text-graph score.
Other languages, jailbreak templates and in-context provision of facts. Emotional and logical framings are reported but not extracted.

missing.what: Recall under emotional and logical framings versus the original prompt. Logical framing raises recall and emotional framing lowers it; framing coefficients are given with M9 held fixed.
Base-model (pre-unlearning) recall per model, domain and framing. Needed to judge how much of the pre-unlearning knowledge prompting restores.
Average recall by algorithm: HP 14.8% WHP vs 13.1% GA+KL; Politicians 30.8% vs 20.0%. Also LLaMA-2-13B Politicians: 55.5→50.6% under WHP vs 29.4% under GA+KL.

record.verdict_notes: Not an original source, though the HP/LLaMA-2-7B WHP model is Eldan & Russinovich's released checkpoint. Recall is LLM-judged percent-factual of open-ended responses, so there is no chance level. Table 10's capability column is shared across algorithms, and the benchmark is unnamed. The intervention rows (i1–i4) are averages over 100 prompts selected for low or high entanglement. Scale correlations use n=4, and only one cell is significant. Persuasive prompts were GPT-4-generated and only spot-checked. The C link was removed because the evidence is a behavioural correlation with a text-graph score, not internal analysis.

versions.untested_parts: The paper measures unlearning suppression, general-capability retention, and recall under rephrased prompts, but does not define or report a chance-level benchmark.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or relearning attack.
No activation-direction ablation; the paper’s evidence is correlational and prompt-intervention evidence about retrieval pathways.
Tests persuasive prompt framing and wording/entanglement changes, not other languages, jailbreaks as a distinct condition, or in-context provision of facts.
No newer counter-method is tested for resistance to these attacks.

relation.reason: Reports how recall changes under rewrites against the direct query on unlearned models.

tranche.reason: Prompt-only attacks (authority framing, entity rewrites) on WHP- and GA+KL-unlearned models. Different method, same question.

source_check.notes: Table 3 gives recall on unlearned models only, with no base-model authority-framed recall, so gains mix recovery with framing's general effect. WHP barely suppressed LLaMA-2-13B on Senators (4.9 pp, §5.4), so p12 is weak recovery evidence. Tables 2 and 3 give no uncertainty. Table 2 uses 100 prompts per domain per set. Table 10's layout is garbled, but the text corroborates it.

statements.correction: §5.4: WHP drops LLaMA-2-13B Senators recall only 4.9 pp (55.5%→50.6%). Table 10: WHP suppression is 5 pp there, against 18 pp on HP. Authority framing on that model: 30.3%→48.7%. The clear recovery cases are GA+KL HP: suppression 34–37 pp; OPT-2.7B 4.3→20.7%, LLaMA-2-7B 9.0→25.3%. Tables 2 and 3 give no uncertainty; SEs and p-values appear only for the regressions (Table 4) and the scale correlations (Table 8).
statements.problem: All numbers match Table 3. But the Senators example (LLaMA-2-13B, WHP) comes from the cell the study says WHP barely unlearned. Its +18.3 pp rise is larger than the ~5 pp that WHP removed, so it is weak evidence of recovering forgotten answers. Also, 'uncertainty' does not apply to the cited numbers.
Values are right and the statement names the single model (LLaMA-2-13B, WHP). Caveat: the domains also differ in how much WHP suppressed that model (HP 18 pp, Senators 5 pp, Table 10).
It makes no claim about this study.
